title: Great yarn
text:
I’ve been knitting for over fifteen years, and I’ve read a lot of pattern books, technique guides, and inspirational collections. When I saw “Great Yarn” is something else entirely. It’s not a pattern book, though it does have dozens already. Instead, it’s a deep, thoughtful exploration of the history, culture, and craft of yarn itself. The author has a gift for storytelling, which is fitting since “yarn” literally means a good tale. Each chapter weaves together the origins of different fibers from sheep farming in the Shetlands to small-batch indigo dyeing in Japan along with profiles of spinners, dyers, and designers I’d never heard of. I learned why some wool feels scratchy and others drape like silk, how yarn thickness is measured internationally, and even the surprising role of yarn-related superstitions from various traditions.

The writing is warm and personal, not dry or academic. It felt like sitting with a knowledgeable friend who just happens to be obsessed with fiber science. The photos are gorgeous, but not just pretty pictures they actually illustrate the text. I’ve already tried two new spinning techniques and a dye method using onion skins after reading about it here. My knitting group passed this around, and everyone came away with something different: one friend started researching local fleece suppliers; another finally understood why her merino pills.

If you love yarn, or if you love great writing about making things, this book belongs on your shelf. It made me appreciate every skein I own just a little more.

text:
I was really excited to get this device, but my excitement turned to frustration within the first week. The worst part by far is the power button. There is no satisfying click when you press it—just a vague, mushy sensation that makes you wonder if you even pressed it at all. I have to jab at it three or four times just to get the screen to turn on, and even then, it sometimes fails to register. It rattles in its housing, which is a constant reminder of the poor build quality.

Beyond the button, the performance is lackluster. It freezes up randomly, and the battery life is nowhere near what was advertised. I fully charged it last night, and it was dead by noon today with minimal use. The software feels half-baked; settings menus lag, and Bluetooth connections drop out constantly. For the price I paid, I expected something that at least functions as a basic electronic device, not a daily frustration.

I am already looking into a replacement, and I will be avoiding this brand entirely. Do yourself a favor and read the other reviews mentioning the power button issue. It is not a minor quirk—it is a design flaw that ruins the entire user experience. Save your money and your sanity. I wish I could return this, but I missed the window by two days.

title: A Christmas treasure
text:
This undiscovered gem of a book has been a Christmastime staple in my family since 1902. Owen Wister is best known for The Virginian, but he makes a major departure from that genre for this book. Set in 13th century England, The Dragon of Wantley is, in Wister's own words, a burlesque. He freely mixes charming anachronisms into his medieval setting. If possible, find the Fourth Edition, which includes several amusing additions, in which Wister takes on some of his literary critics.

I have now bought 5 copies of this book, as well as the one I inherited from my father. Buy it, treasure it and pass it along. Some day, I hope, the BBC will make a film version of it. Read it, and see if you agree that Brian Blessed was born to play the Lord of Wantley Manor.

title: Should Be a Movie
text:
I picked up Should Be a Movie because the premise — a story so cinematic it feels like a screenplay waiting to happen — sounded irresistible, and for the most part the book delivers exactly that kind of experience. From the opening chapter I was immediately swept into lush, vividly described scenes that felt staged for a wide-screen adaptation: sweeping locations, sharp, witty dialogue, and a cast of characters who are equal parts charming and flawed.

The narrator’s voice is one of the book’s biggest strengths. There’s a self-aware, slightly sardonic tone that kept me smiling aloud on the subway and turning pages faster than I meant to. The protagonist is likable without being perfect; their internal monologue balances humor with genuine vulnerability, which made it easy to root for them even when their choices were messy. Secondary characters are well-drawn and memorable — a friend who steals every scene with deadpan one-liners, a love interest with complicated motives, and a rival who’s both infuriating and oddly relatable.

Pacing is generally strong. The middle section unspooled like a montage: set-ups, missteps, reconciliations, and a few surprises that kept me engaged. There are moments of quiet reflection that add emotional depth, and then the narrative will snap back into high-energy sequences that feel cinematic in the best way. The author’s knack for visual detail makes many scenes pop — I could see the city lights, hear the background music, and almost feel the weather on the characters’ skin.

That said, the book isn’t flawless. A couple of plot threads felt a bit underdeveloped, leaving me wanting more explanation about certain character motivations. And the ending, while satisfying, leans a little towards neatness; I would have enjoyed a touch more ambiguity or risk. A few sentences occasionally veered into purple prose, breaking the otherwise crisp rhythm, but those instances were infrequent.

Overall, Should Be a Movie is an entertaining, well-written read that will particularly delight anyone who loves contemporary fiction with strong dialogue and cinematic flair. It’s the kind of book you’ll want to recommend to friends and — yes — imagine being adapted for the screen. I’m giving it four stars because it’s consistently enjoyable and emotionally engaging, even if a little tightening in places would have made it exceptional.

text:
I bought this sling hoping it would be an affordable, authentic-feeling replacement for the tired, cracked leather piece on my Mosin Nagant 91/30, and it exceeded my expectations. Functionally it performs exactly as advertised — a dependable field sling that feels period-appropriate. title: Flyover Nation- A window into our country's soul.
text:
I bought this book as a gift for my father, who has spent his entire adult life working in the industrial Midwest. It was a challenging subject, as his community often feels misunderstood or overlooked by coastal media narratives, but this book handles the topic with such profound empathy and journalistic integrity that it resonated deeply with him. The author does not offer easy answers or cheap political talking points. Instead, he takes the time to truly listen to the people living in the flyover states, capturing their fears, their dignity, and their complex relationship with modern America.

The narrative structure is compelling, weaving personal anecdotes with broader economic and cultural analysis without ever feeling academic or detached. I found myself reading late into the night, genuinely moved by the human stories at the center of the argument. It is rare to find a work that challenges you to think differently without being preachy. My father actually set it down multiple times to reflect on passages, which rarely happens with non-fiction. This is not just a book about politics; it is a testament to the resilience of the American spirit. It has sparked meaningful conversations at our dinner table about topics we usually avoid. If you are looking for a nuanced, heart-wrenching, and ultimately hopeful look at what makes this country tick, this is essential reading. It deserves every star and more for its courage and clarity.

title: Very happy to finally lay hands on one it is now ...
text:
Very happy to finally lay hands on one it is now sitting in my game room next to my other favorites. I have been watching this item come back in and out of stock for months, and every time I hesitated, it vanished before I could check out. When I saw the restock notification this time, I jumped on it immediately, and I am so glad I did.

I am writing this review after three full plays with a group of four adults, plus one solo run to learn the rules. The components are absolutely gorgeous – the card stock is thick with a linen finish that feels premium, the tokens are chunky, and the artwork on everything is vibrant without being overly busy. The rulebook is clearly laid out, which is a huge relief because I have had to teach many complicated games that required constant rule lookups. This one took about ten minutes to explain, and by the second round everyone was strategizing on their own.

What really sets this game apart is the balance between luck and planning. You can have a perfect strategy, but a few unlucky draws can push you to adapt on the fly, which keeps every session fresh. The replay value seems immense. There are multiple character abilities, variable setup options, and a scoring system that rewards different play styles – aggressive builders, cautious explorers, and even sneaky traders all have viable paths to victory. My last game came down to a single point, and the table erupted into friendly arguments about who should have blocked whom. That is the mark of a great game.

The only minor criticism I have is that the box insert could be a little more efficient; the plastic trays leave some pieces loose if you store it vertically. But that is a small nitpick for such a well-crafted product. For anyone on the fence, do not wait. This one sells out fast for a reason, and I can already tell it will be hitting our table regularly for years to come. If you love medium-weight strategy games with a bit of social interaction, this is a must-buy. Five stars without hesitation.

title: A fun political satire and much more…
text:
The First Lady Escapes is obviously a satire of the current political atmosphere, but it is also an enjoyable, well thought-out story with a fun cast of characters. As I was reading the story, I found myself falling in love with several of them, especially Angel, the gay Mexican hairdresser, and Moon, a FLOTUS impersonator, and I was eagerly anticipating what would happen as each new chapter began. The short chapters are titled with a location and time to add to the fun so the reader can feel the excitement build as events unfold simultaneously at the White House and across the US and Mexico.

While the President is the focus of the political satire, FLOTUS and the characters who become part of her journey are well-developed and bring the story to life. The detailed descriptions of their surroundings and activities made me feel like I was escaping to Mexico with FLOTUS or part of the White House luxury being experienced for the first time by FLOTUS’ impersonator.

I picked up this book because I was intrigued by the premise and hoped for a few moments of escapism from the daily news. I got that and so much more. The author acknowledges the current political situation inspired her to write this satire, but beyond that initial premise, she created an entertaining story with well developed characters that evolve to show the people behind traditional stereotypes whether they are immigrants, paparazzi, or transgender. This is definitely not a read for supporters of the current administration. But for everyone else who has felt concern, frustration, or outrage as they read the latest news feeds, this book will put a smile on your face and even let you laugh out loud and be entertained for a few fun hours.

title: One of the most enlightening books on politics from the ...
text:
I rarely write reviews, but this book compelled me to sit down and share how profoundly it changed my understanding of politics. From the first chapter I felt like someone had taken the noise out of the room and handed me a clear map. The author explains complex ideas with patience and real-world examples, making abstract theories feel relevant to everyday decisions and debates.

What I appreciated most was the balance: this is not polemic or partisan sloganeering. Instead, it's an invitation to think critically about institutions, incentives, and the incentives of the people who operate within them. The historical context and case studies are carefully chosen and well-researched, yet rendered in an approachable style that never talks down to the reader. I learned new frameworks for evaluating policy proposals and interpreting political behavior, and those frameworks have already changed how I read the news and discuss politics with friends.

The book is also practical — it offers tools for civic engagement that are realistic rather than utopian, which I found refreshingly honest. If you care about understanding why political systems behave as they do and want to be better informed (not just louder), this is one of the most enlightening books on the subject I've read. Highly recommended.

title: When Simple Faith is Simply Not Enough
text:
"Today, twenty-first century theology tends to make religion a belief based upon faith rather than a belief of faith based upon fact. History, science, and conflicting Scriptures are all too often dismissed when they conflict with accepted creeds or dogma. Most Judeo-Christians are taught there are certain areas of their religion they should not question, causing the phrase “it is a matter of faith” to be well-worn and overused.
Scripture encourages individuals to question their idea of God."
And question it she did!
For Jodell Onstott, like so many of us, simple faith was simply not enough. Unable to dismiss the passionate; yet, conflicting views of countless denominations… the seemingly endless interpretations of a single text… the bearing of historic facts and archeological discoveries… the consequence of scientific evidences… Jodell embarked upon a decade long mission to discover the not so simple truth. And though the title of the subsequent book, “YHVH Exists” may eliminate the suspense of her ultimate conclusion, Jodell’s journey is a masterpiece of well-organized testimonies and closely examined proofs. Leaving no stone unturned, her systematic examination of the data demonstrates a sincere desire to reach an objective opinion.
The long-awaited “YHVH Exists” is a thorough and fascinating study that will challenge your most hidden preconceptions, and, may well find itself on the more than one bestseller’s list in the process.
Well worth the wait!

I miss the old days wear quality mattered - I can't buy a children's game, or even a t-shirt - that has any quality craftsmanship about it. I'm really tired of cheap and crappy stuff.

Yes, the connecting parts could be a little tighter; a few of them pop off if you push too hard. But that also meant he had to figure out how to balance and adjust, so maybe that’s a feature, not a bug. The set includes enough pieces to build a few different configurations, and he’s already asking for an expansion pack. The colors are bright, the box is compact for storage, and nothing broke during the first week of use. For the price, we got a small plastic shavings from a couple of the snap-together joints, but I just wiped them off and no harm done. For the moment you open the box. For the price, this set does everything a parent wants: it keeps the kid entertained, encourages a minimal amount of adult intervention, and it doesn’t fall apart after one session. It’s a house. It’s not the premium brand with magnetic precision engineering, but for a day-in, day-out toy that a child will actually play with instead of tossing aside after ten minutes, this fits the bill perfectly. I would buy it again for another kid, and I might even pick up a second set for my own son when he’s a little older. title: A Classic with a contemporary interpretation
text:
Not much needs to be said here about the story of this truly perennial classic. The War of the Worlds (1898) is the account of Martians invading earth, attacking and ruining London. What happens to the rest of earth and mankind is not resolved till the very end. Although this novel was seen as the start of modern science fiction, it had also a deeper meaning of fighting tyrannies and the occurrence of mass-hysteria.

This deeper meaning was clearly shown when Orson Wells broadcast in 1938 an extremely believable radio dramatization. Listeners thought that Martians were actually attacking and in panic they left their homes trying to escape this terrifying experience. It is interesting to note that that broadcast happened at the eve of World War II.

Now in 2005, a new movie adaption has just been released by Steven Spielberg and starring Tom Cruise. While I'll leave it to movie critics to evaluate that movie, it has already received wide acclaim for its special effects. Something else interesting to note is that in the early scenes of the attack by the Martians, the children of the character played by Cruise question whether these are attacks by "terrorists". In an era where we are sandwiched in time by 9/11, the wars in Iraq and Afghanistan, and further terrorist attacks in Bali, Istanbul, Madrid and London, the world seems again in the grip of fear, of wars and of mass-hysteria. One could wonder if The War of the Worlds in 2005 again will create or foresee further scares in the world.

What makes this edition of The War of the Worlds so worthwhile is not just the inclusion of the classic illustrations by Henrique Alvin Correa, but also the introduction by Robert Bartholomew. Bartholomew is a leading expert on panic attacks, media manipulation and mass delusion, and he puts this book in historical and contemporary context. He tries to answer why this book has "created" such a scare in 1898, in 1938 and maybe again in 2005, or is the scare in all of us us calling this book into everlasting existence? I rate this edition 4 stars, and just wished that the publisher had considered releasing a hard cover edition.

title: Just one question:  Why?
text:
In five editions (and counting of the Physical Basis for the Direction of Time) Dieter Zee has been asking the same question: What laws of the universe are actually law like and what laws of the universe are merely fact like?

This is a question very much at the heart of this brief accessible tome wherein Great Britain's Royal Astronomer probes the significance of two microscopic numbers and four macroscopic numbers that seem to effect the raison d'etre of the universe.

Along the way we deal with claims such as the cosmic anthropologic hypothesis which assert that the universe was created specifically the way it was in order to allow life (an assertion a little like Goldfish saying that the aquarium in which they live and the country house that supports it was created specifically for them).

Things happen and unless you're Paul Davies and writing any of his major works on the matter (starting with God and the New Physics proceeding to the award winning Mind of God and finally concluding with the hard back title Cosmic Jackpot) we are merely "a thing that happened."

Humbling no doubt but a likely consequence of fraction of a fraction of fraction of...you get the point...of our occupying the merest miniscule part of creation.

But this book is important reading. Like any good reporting it lays out the conventional wisdom (of 1999, still sadly all too current in 2009) and leaves the reader to decide.

Why? In it's ultimate sense the question will always remain a personal one. But at least science can say, and purport to actually prove, that we're in there somewhere.

title: Great value, particularly for the accessories
text:
Fortnite's figures are great, and collecting accessories is much of the fun, but you don't usually get many accessories with basic figures--you typically either have to buy loot chests or special/deluxe sets to get accessories. The piñatas are some of the best deals due to how many accessories you get, along with a figure. Although the MSRP of a piñata is slightly higher than the price of a single figure plus a single loot chest, you get a lot more content--over twice as many accessories as what you'd get from a standard loot chest. And not all the accessories or variations can be found in other sets--so even if you already have a decent stash of accessories, some of these will probably still be new to you.

The Rust Lord figure is not the prettiest or fanciest-looking figure in the series, but he's pretty decent. A lot of the characters are very cartoony, but this guy's design is a little bit more subdued, which may or may not be a plus depending on your tastes. Like all the 4" figures, he's got a very high amount of articulation and pretty sophisticated construction, so you'll want to be a little careful with him at first. If any joints seem stuck, try soaking him in hot water briefly to loosen them up and lessen the risk of breakage. I haven't had any problems with any of my figures yet, but be aware it can happen. I wouldn't recommend these for very young kids due to their relatively complex design.

And yes, the packaging is really a sort of piñata. It's designed for you to be able to bash it open. You can probably open it up without destroying it if you are careful. Be aware that there's a lot of confetti inside, in case you do decide to break it open.

title: Sweet, slow, sad
text:
Thin Wood Walls follows young Joe Hanada's family experiences during the time of WWII. After the bombing of Pearl Harbor, Joe's father is taken away by the FBI as a person of suspicion because he is a community leader. The rest of the family, including Joe's feisty grandmother and more feisty big brother Mike, are taken to Tule Lake Relocation Camp and must adjust to a new life while anxiously awaiting the return of the father.

Not much happens in the book, as camp life is boredom, waiting, hoping, but Joe tries to make do and make sense of what is happening while fearing what his big brother intends to do. The story is balanced, showing how not all white Americans were against the Japanese in the U.S. Some Japanese were very angry while many exhibited a sad stoicism. Perhaps what sets this book apart from other internment stories is that it is set in the Tule Lake camp, which was where troublemakers, the "no-no's" and those wanting to return to Japan were sent. This created a turbulent, sometimes dangerous atmosphere that other camps did not experience, at least not on that level. Thin Wood Walls delves into this in a manner suitable for middle-graders.

The book is a bit slow, but sweet, the writing rather plain despite the bits of haiku, but this will appeal to boys as well as girls and provide a thoughtful look at the sad facts of this long-hidden part of U.S. history. Expect a tear at the end, and be sure to read the Author's Notes.

[[ASIN:0939165538 Looking Like the Enemy: My Story of Imprisonment in Japanese American Internment Camps]] is also set in Tule Lake, but is a true story. A Young Reader's edition is coming out in Fall 2010.

title: Nice laptop for the price.
text:
I bought this laptop about two months ago after needing an affordable replacement for my aging machine, and I’m really impressed with the value it delivers. Right out of the box setup was straightforward — Windows walked me through updates and drivers installed without any extra hassle. The build feels solid for the price point; the chassis isn’t premium metal, but it’s sturdy with no flex and the hinge is tight and reliable.

Performance has been more than adequate for my day-to-day needs. I use it for web browsing with many tabs open, streaming, office work, video calls, and light photo editing. The processor handles multitasking smoothly and I haven’t experienced any slowdowns for these tasks. Battery life comfortably lasts me a workday with moderate use — typically around 6–7 hours — so I can take it on the go without needing frequent charging. Charging is reasonably quick as well.

The display is clear and bright enough for indoor use; colors are decent for casual photo editing and watching videos, though it’s not a professional-grade panel. Keyboard typing feels comfortable with good key travel, and the touchpad is responsive and accurate. Built-in speakers are fine for casual listening; I use headphones for better audio when watching movies.

There are a couple of small downsides: the webcam is average and low-light performance could be better, and the preinstalled bloatware required a quick cleanup. Otherwise, this laptop gives a lot of functionality for the money. If you need a reliable, budget-friendly laptop for everyday tasks, this is an excellent choice. I’d buy it again.

Dr. Kate English is a member of east coast high-society, but her world is turned upside down when her mother is brutally murdered with no explanation. The one good thing that comes from it all is Kate's ex-best friend, Blaire Barrington, returns to attend the funeral.

Blaire and Kate are on the road to mending fences when Kate begins receiving threatening text messages in the form of murderess nursery rhymes. As her search for her mother's killer takes over her life the private lives of her social circle begin to unravel tales of deceit, lying and infidelity.

title: An Unexpected LOVE!!!
text:
I rarely write reviews, but this book compelled me to share how much it moved me. I bought An Unexpected LOVE!!! on a quiet Sunday afternoon and finished it in two sittings — something I haven't done in years. The characters felt like friends I hadn't met yet: flawed, honest, and achingly real. The author's voice is warm and candid, striking a perfect balance between humor and heartache. Dialogue is natural and often had me smiling out loud.

What surprised me most was how the story grew beyond a simple romance. It explored family dynamics, second chances, and the messy work of rebuilding trust without ever feeling forced or preachy. The pacing is excellent; there are tender, slow-burning moments and scenes that genuinely took my breath away. I appreciated that the protagonists were given space to grow individually rather than the plot hinging solely on a whirlwind attraction.

The writing is crisp and evocative — I could picture every setting, from the cozy café where they met to the stormy night that changed everything. Secondary characters are well-drawn and added depth to the story rather than serving as mere plot devices. The ending was satisfying and hopeful without being predictable.

If you enjoy contemporary romance with emotional depth, authentic characters, and smart, heartfelt storytelling, this book is a gem. I will definitely be recommending it to friends and returning to it again — a rare treat that felt like a warm, unexpected hug.

The aesthetic appeal is decent, and it looks nice on the shelf once fully assembled, but it doesn't have that premium feel that I associate with higher-end brands. For casual play or as a one-time gift, it might suffice, but for serious collectors or everyday robust use, I would hesitate to recommend it. There are better alternatives out there that offer more stability and clearer instructions for a similar cost. I used this for about a week, and while it served its purpose, it didn't bring the joy or engagement I anticipated. It is an okay product that does the job adequately but fails to exceed expectations in any significant way. If you are looking for something to fill time for a few hours, it will work. However, if you want longevity and high-quality construction, you might want to spend a little more on a different brand. My final verdict is that it is an average product with neither strong highs nor catastrophic lows.

text: We have a large-breed dog (Akita) Rescue and wash lots of dog bowls. We first fell in love with Scrub Daddy because you can use it over and over again with no mildew smell. At first, we were willing to forgive the high price for the little happy face on "daddy" but rather quickly, too quickly, in fact, his face went from happy to sad. In fact, he was downright distraught while sitting on the counter and he flopped around in our hand making it difficult to use. We then stumbled on the Lunatec. Yes, it's a little different. Like a dish cloth but ...more...nylon-netty and flimsy. But that's what makes it perfect! The Luncatec can lay across a finger tip and wipe inside a water bottle or other small area, lay flat and wash out a large water trough or bowl, or, fold it in half or quarters for a scrub-pad effect. A Scrub Buddy, with average use (used twice a day on 6 bowls) lasted about 2 weeks. So far, the Lunatec has been here and after nearly 3 weeks, shows ZERO signs of wear. No smell, no scudge, no bacteria. Just clean, clean, scrubbing and clean clean bowls. Oh, we noted another reviewer was unhappy with the Lunatec because he said he washed out a bowl with bread dough and it clogged the Lunatec. Well, duh, or, should we say "Doh!" You should expect that result with ANY type of sponge or cloth and a gooey/gummy dough. When we make bread or macaroni and cheese and have gooey bowls, we use plastic pan scrapers or a hard sink brush to knock off all the gooey/gummy stuff first and then use a sponge or cloth to do the washing/sanitizing. One Scrub Daddy for $8.50 or FOUR (4) Lunatec's for $7.50. The choice is simple, we think. This product stands up, does MORE than it should, and for that, we love you, you Lunatec!

title: Where's the apricot?
text:
I finally decided to treat myself to a proper facial moisturizer after years of neglecting my skin barrier due to stress and harsh weather conditions. The packaging of Where's the apricot? is quite striking, with its minimalist white bottle and simple typography that immediately suggests a clean, clinical approach to skincare. This aesthetic alone was enough to make me confident that I was making a sensible investment in my daily routine. The product arrived quickly and was well-protected, which is always a relief when ordering fragile glass containers online.

Upon opening the bottle, the first thing I noticed was the scent. It has a very distinct, fresh aroma that reminds me slightly of citrus but with a subtle nutty undertone, likely from the apricot kernel oil mentioned on the label. It is not overpowering or perfumed in a way that feels artificial. Instead, it smells natural and inviting, which sets a pleasant tone for my morning skincare ritual. I have combination skin, which means I usually struggle to find a moisturizer that hydrates without making my T-zone look greasy by midday. This product has managed to strike a surprising balance.

I have been using it consistently for about three weeks now. The texture is lightweight and absorbs into the skin relatively quickly, leaving behind a soft, supple finish rather than a heavy, occlusive layer. I noticed a significant improvement in the dryness around my nose and cheeks, areas that usually flare up during colder months. My skin feels more resilient and less reactive to environmental changes. However, I am giving this product four stars instead of five for one specific reason. While the hydration is excellent, I found that for my oily zones, I might need to use a slightly lighter layer or perhaps pair it with a mattifying powder during the day to maintain shine control. It works well, but it requires a bit of adjustment depending on where you apply it on your face.

The ingredients list is transparent and reassuring, focusing on natural oils and gentle botanicals. I appreciate that there are no harsh sulfates or artificial fragrances cluttering the formula. For anyone looking for a straightforward, effective moisturizer that does exactly what it promises without unnecessary gimmicks, this is a strong contender. It is not a miracle worker that will erase years of sun damage overnight, but it is a reliable staple for maintaining healthy, hydrated skin. The price point is reasonable for the quality of the formula, and I expect to repurchase this once I finish the current bottle. It has earned its place on my bathroom shelf as a consistent, trustworthy part of my regimen.

title: Thin
text:
I wish I could give this product zero stars because it genuinely disappointed me on multiple levels. I bought the "Thin" line of dietary supplements with high hopes, expecting a subtle, perhaps unnoticeable shift in my lifestyle that would lead to results. Instead, I found myself dealing with a product that felt more like a placebo with a premium price tag attached to it. From the moment I opened the bottle, the quality was questionable. The capsules had a strange, overly powdery texture that suggested poor manufacturing standards, which immediately put me on edge regarding the actual ingredients inside.

The marketing claims were aggressive, promising noticeable thinning of fat layers within weeks without rigorous exercise or dietary changes. Let me be clear: there was nothing noticeable. I followed the instructions precisely, taking the recommended dosage every single day for four weeks. During this time, I also monitored my caloric intake and maintained my usual activity levels, so any change should have been detectable. There was none. In fact, I felt slightly more bloated in the mornings, which was the opposite of the intended effect.

Customer service was equally frustrating. When I reached out to ask if this was normal, I received a generic, automated response that offered no real solution or explanation. It felt like they were just trying to silence a complaint rather than address a potential issue with the batch. I checked online forums and found several other users reporting the same lack of efficacy, which confirms that this isn’t just bad luck on my part.

The cost is another major factor. For the price of one bottle, I could have purchased a gym membership for two months or hired a nutritionist for a consultation. Those resources would have likely yielded better, healthier, and more sustainable results than this overhyped supplement. It is clear that the brand is spending more on advertising than on effective formulation. I do not recommend this to anyone looking for genuine health improvements. Save your money and invest in whole foods and physical activity instead. This product is a waste of cash and time, and I will not be repurchasing it under any circumstances.

title: Hard to assemble
text:
I bought this for my seven-year-old’s birthday, thinking it would be a fun afternoon project we could do together. The concept is great and the final product, once it’s actually came together, did look pretty cool. My son was thrilled with the moving the pieces around immediately and that part was fine. The problem-free. The instructions, though, are where things fell apart. They are printed in such a tiny font with diagrams that look like they were photocopied three times. Several steps are ambiguous, and there is no indication of which side is up or which piece goes where until you’ve already forced something in the wrong direction.

I am not a stranger to putting together toys and furniture, but this one tested my patience. Some of the plastic connectors required a lot of pressure to snap into place, and I was genuinely worried I would break a tab. There are also small pieces that need to be inserted at just the right angle, and if you miss, the adult, miss that angle, the whole thing refuses to click. I ended up redoing three steps because I thought I had it right the first time. It took nearly two hours, whereas the box implied about 30 minutes. 

For the price, I expected a smoother experience. Once assembled, my child loves playing with it, but I would not buy this again for someone who does not enjoy a lot of spare time or patience. The design is clever design is undermined by the frustrating build. Three stars because the end result is decent, but the fun I expected, but the journey to get there was a two-hour headache that I could have done without. If you buy this, set aside plenty of time and maybe have a pair of pliers handy for those stubborn joints.

While the general romantic template is present (i.e. girl falls in love, girl thinks love is impossible, girl fights for love, etc) Cornwell's talent for intricate plot lines, complex villains, and sudden plot twists are present as well.  There were a few times in reading when the sudden switch from Campion's rosy love-filled perspective to a more jaded viewpoint (usually ending in someone's sudden and brutal death) was a little jarring, but on the whole it was still the type of read I expect when I pick up Cornwell's books- A little softer around the edges maybe, but still crafted with his trademark knack for historical realism and ripping good yarns.

title: OK
text:
I bought this OK fitness tracker a few weeks ago after reading some mixed reviews and wanting something affordable to monitor steps and sleep. Overall I’m moderately satisfied — it does many things adequately but nothing outstanding.

Setup was straightforward and the companion app is simple to navigate, though a bit slow to sync at times. Step counting seems reasonably accurate for daily walks, but it occasionally misses short indoor steps or counts arm movements as steps when I’m doing dishes. Heart rate monitoring works well during steady-state cardio but lags during interval workouts and sometimes shows spikes that don’t match how I feel.

Battery life met the advertised claim; I got about five days between charges with regular use and notifications enabled. The band is comfortable enough for everyday wear and the display is readable in daylight, though a bit dim indoors at the lowest setting.

I appreciate the sleep-tracking feature, but the sleep stages feel approximate and sometimes label restless nights inaccurately. Customer support responded politely when I had a sync issue, but resolution took a few days.

If you want a budget-friendly tracker with basic features, this is fine. If you need highly accurate metrics for serious training, consider a step up.

title: Another Gem
text: First off, knowing how to play the basic triads for the the 4 primary scales, major, harmonic major, harmonic minor and melodic minor in 4 string groups is a helpful instigator of original ideas. The inversions that skip strings sound even better. I like the inversions using the two forms on the first 5 strings, Vic prefers strings 6,4 and 3. Then you are given moveable roots to go along with these triad inversions that give mini alteration flavor. Next up are traditional 4 note chords and their inversions of which you must learn the most common alterations.  Vic then goes into areas of stacked triad and modal harmony which give the book it's 'advanced' rating, Fascinating stuff for sure. To come up with these ideas and relationships on your own would be very tuff unless you were an unrelenting genius with resources. He concludes with chord charts of various voicings that include open strings . There is tab but it's only used to clarify suggested fingerings. To get the most out of this book you would need to be a student of music but there's nothing stuffy or drawn out about the presentation. He points out useful scalic relationships for the modal chord forms and many musical examples of the concepts presented. It seems more essential theory than White Elephant Theory . I'd take this one with me to a desert island because many musical questions are answered pragmatically and unselfishlessly. With this and the Slonimsky interval bible, you could create brand new forms of music to entertain the crabs.

title: A fun way to explore language
text: This is a book I would have loved to have as a child. It's not the kind of book you just sit down and read cover to cover, it's more like a very specialized dictionary. The author has curated a list of words--four for each letter of the alphabet--and explains how it is used and how it came to be used. As the author notes in the introduction, words have personalities, and this book explores them. Did you ever wonder why a British policeman is called a Bobby? Why the yellow weeds we see everywhere are called dandelions? Why long races are called marathons or why it's called a quarantine when people are kept separate from others? This book explains all these words and many more, including some that are definitely not in the average grade school vocabulary. Although the book is published in the United States, there are many words used more commonly in Great Britain and a fair amount that may seem a bit archaic, but readers still learn about everyday words like pajamas and shampoo. It's a great choice for encouraging creativity, enlarging and enriching a child's vocabulary, and for that kiddo that just loves knowing all sorts of off-beat and fascinating facts. Grownups reading along with them should be prepared to be surprised and educated, too.

title: Needs a lot of drying time
text:
I wanted to like this product — the packaging looked nice and the shade matched what I expected from the photos. I'm giving it three stars because it has both positives and drawbacks that are worth knowing before you buy.

First the good: the formula goes on smoothly and provides decent coverage once it's fully dry. It doesn't have a strong chemical smell, and I didn't experience any irritation on my skin. After it set, my makeup looked fairly natural and the finish was pleasant — not overly matte or greasy. It also lasted a reasonable part of the day without needing constant touch-ups.

Now the big caveat: the drying time. It takes much longer to fully set than I anticipated. I followed the instructions, and while the product felt tacky for a long time, it didn't truly dry for nearly twice as long as similar items I’ve used. That meant I had to be extra careful getting dressed, putting on jewelry, or touching my hair. A few times it transferred onto my scarf and sleeve despite trying to be careful. If you’re in a hurry most mornings, this will be frustrating.

Another small issue is that if you try to layer it before it’s fully dry, it pills and becomes uneven. I learned to apply a thinner layer and wait patiently, but that reduced the coverage and required a second coat with more drying time.

Overall, it’s an okay product if you plan ahead and don’t need something quick. Good finish and tolerable wear, but the long drying time and transfer risk keep it from being a favorite. I’d recommend it only to people who can spare the extra time for application.

title: Highest Quality
text:
I’ve been using this Highest Quality set in my kitchen for a few weeks now and honestly it’s been a game changer. From the moment I unpacked it the materials felt substantial and well-made — no flimsy plastic or cheap finishes. The pieces are thoughtfully designed: handles are comfortable, weight is balanced, and everything cleans up easily without staining. I’ve cooked soups, roasted vegetables, and even baked with it, and each time performance was consistent. The heat distribution is excellent and nothing stuck during searing or sautéing, which saved me a lot of time and frustration.

The set also looks great on the counter; the finish has held up without scratching or dulling. Storage is straightforward and doesn’t take up excess space. After multiple dishwasher cycles the look and function remain unchanged. Customer service was responsive when I had a small question about care instructions, which I appreciated. For the price, this is one of the best kitchen purchases I’ve made recently — durable, reliable, and truly high quality. Highly recommended.

title: Perfect Christmas gift.
text:
I bought this as a Christmas gift for my assistant, who is constantly complains about the clutter on her desk attracts. I’ll be honest, I wasn’t expecting much from an office product under twenty dollars, but this little organizer has genuinely impressed both of us.

The packaging arrived well before the holiday, and the box itself looked nice enough to go right under the tree. When she opened it, she actually laughed and said, “You get me.” The build quality is solid—surprisingly—sturdy, not flimsy at all. The compartments are well-sized: the larger slots fit her tablet and a standard notepad, while the smaller dividers hold pens, sticky notes, and her business card case without everything jumbling together. The non-slip base keeps it planted on her desk even a cluttered desk corner, which was a detail I didn’t expect but she now appreciates.

She’s been using it for about three weeks now, and she told me last Friday that her workspace has never been this organized. She even stopped misplacing her glasses. For the price, this is an absolute steal. It’s professional enough for a corporate office but also looks great in a home workspace.

If you’re looking for a practical, thoughtful gift for a coworker, boss, or anyone who spends time at a desk, I cannot recommend this enough. It’s the kind of gift that shows you pay attention to their daily frustrations. Five stars, no question.

title: I'M SENDING THIS BACK; VERY DISAPPOINTED
text:
I bought this hoping it would solve a simple problem in my kitchen, but it has been nothing but frustration. Right out of the box the finish was uneven and there were scuff marks that looked like it had been returned before. The instructions are vague and missing key details — it took me twice as long to assemble because the parts don’t line up as shown. Once assembled it doesn’t function as advertised: the latch sticks, one of the fittings is loose, and it wobbles when you put even a light item on it.

Materials feel cheap and flimsy, not what the product description led me to expect. I emailed customer service about the defects and got an automated response that didn’t address any of my concerns. No offer to replace or refund, just a link to their FAQ. For the price I paid I expected sturdier construction and better support.

I also noticed the dimensions were off by a couple of inches compared to the listing, which meant it didn’t fit where I planned to put it. That alone is a deal-breaker for me. Packing was minimal and things shifted during shipping, which likely contributed to the visible damage.

I’m returning this and would not recommend it. Save yourself the hassle and look for something with better reviews and clearer specs. If you care about build quality and accurate descriptions, this is not the product to buy. Very disappointed.
